w1_final.reason: Current message reports a new Chinese National Public Procurement Administration notice (No. 18 of 2027) establishing a memory-component eligibility review for designated data-infrastructure projects, with confirmed cancellations of pending Micron releases. None of the loaded events cover this: E117 is U.S. policy restricting Apple from sourcing Chinese memory; E111 is Citi's analyst view on Chinese supply pressure; E31 is generic trade-rule anxiety. The concrete Chinese procurement action and its direct effect on Micron supply are entirely new core facts.

candidates.proposition: China's National Public Procurement Administration issued Notice No. 18 of 2027 establishing a mandatory eligibility review for memory components used in designated data-infrastructure projects, taking effect May 21, 2027.

Purchasing entities responsible for designated data-infrastructure projects must complete an eligibility review before placing, renewing, or releasing purchase orders for high-reliability memory modules, solid-state storage components, and integrated memory assemblies listed in Annex III.
Project operators must complete a review of all open procurement records within ten working days, examining pending purchase releases against Annex III product and project descriptions.
candidates.subject_time: Within ten working days after effective date

candidates.proposition: The Administration received implementation reports identifying cancellations of pending Micron memory-component releases associated with designated data-infrastructure projects.
The implementation reports identified movement of the cancelled Micron requirements to alternative approved supply arrangements.

The reports do not identify a common product code, common customer name, or common reason for each Micron cancellation; each operator must preserve its own review record and cite Annex III wording when notifying suppliers.
The notice explicitly does not direct operators to halt operating systems or remove installed equipment.

Annex III defines covered projects as including public-cloud data-service projects and 'other corresponding infrastructure uses,' and the operative list includes formulations not reproduced in earlier public summaries.
